title: Decoding the cancer microbiome: multi-omics; AI; and translational opportunities.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Pulled the full open-access text (140 KB) and its data availability statement, which reads verbatim 'No datasets were generated or analysed during the current study.' Downloaded the Europe PMC supplementary bundle (0.17 MB): it contains only two copies of Figure 1 (a GIF and a WEBP image), no tables and no data files. Grepped the whole text for github, zenodo, figshare, dryad and gitlab links: zero hits. Ran a Zenodo/Dryad search on the DOI: no deposits.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The accession numbers found by text mining (GEO series GSE17536, GSE17537, GSE72970, GSE161158; sequencing projects PRJEB22863, PRJEB22893, PRJNA397906, PRJNA399742, PRJNA541981) appear only inside the review's narrative summary tables, where they cite other groups' published studies. I did not open those third-party archives because they belong to other papers and are mostly raw sequencing.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL and fatal. This is a narrative review article, not a data paper. The data availability statement states no datasets were generated or analysed, the supplement is two image files of Figure 1, and there is no code or data repository anywhere in the text. There is nothing to download.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. No table of labels exists. The only structured content is five in-text narrative tables summarising other people's findings (roughly a dozen distinct source studies, judged by the PubMed identifiers cited in them). Any modelling target would have to be constructed from scratch by re-downloading and reprocessing a dozen external raw-sequencing archives.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. Inputs exist only as pointers: GEO series identifiers and sequencing-project identifiers for other labs' RNA sequencing, whole-genome sequencing and 16S ribosomal RNA gene sequencing runs. Nothing is present in the paper itself.

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable, no measurement table exists.

a5_enough_rows.note: Not applicable. The in-text summary tables hold at most a few dozen rows of free-text association claims, far below the ~400-row minimum, and they are prose summaries rather than measurements.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits, because there is nothing but text and two figure images. Assembling the cited third-party archives instead would mean terabytes of raw sequencing, which CLAUDE.md forbids downloading.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable: there are no counts and no files to compare them against.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not applicable here, but worth recording: the dominant public label source in this subfield, the Cancer Genome Atlas microbiome tables from Poore et al. 2020, was retracted in 2024 after Gihawi et al. showed the microbial read counts were inflated by contamination and human-sequence mismatches, so labels derived from it are unsafe.

existing_models.name: Poore et al. 2020 Cancer Genome Atlas microbiome classifiers (gradient boosting and random forest on tumour-derived microbial read counts)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported 95-100 percent accuracy discriminating each of 32 cancer types against all others, on 17,625 samples; the paper was retracted from Nature in 2024 after a reanalysis showed most of the signal came from contamination and human-read misassignment.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Decontamination and batch correction of tumour sequencing data; the retraction and the Gihawi et al. rebuttal make this the central open problem of the field.

existing_models.name: BreCol (2026 preprint benchmark of classical and deep-learning methods for microbiome-based cancer detection)
existing_models.score_and_split: 2,040 16S ribosomal RNA sequencing runs over 26 studies; classical models reach test/holdout area under the curve of 0.77/0.60 for cancer diagnosis and 1.00/0.83 for cancer-type prediction, with holdout being studies from 2023 onward. It also evaluates HyenaDNA (a long-range DNA sequence model) and SetBERT (a transformer over sets of sequencing reads).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: The large drop from test to holdout area under the curve, i.e. generalisation across studies, is explicitly the unsolved part.

existing_models.name: Colorectal-cancer faecal microbiome pipeline benchmark (Microbiome Research Reports 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: 4,217 faecal samples across global cohorts, 6,468 analytical pipelines compared; shotgun metagenomics beat 16S, and eXtreme Gradient Boosting plus random forest were the best classifiers.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Choice of preprocessing pipeline dominates the result, so cross-cohort comparability remains unresolved.

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: No join is possible because the paper contributes no table with identifiers in it.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible from this paper: it is a review with no data of its own, so any model would in fact be built on other groups' archives and would have to be evaluated against those papers, not this one.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use microbes detected inside tumours to predict cancer type and response to immunotherapy.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would use microbial abundance profiles per tumour or stool sample, from the third-party archives this review cites (four gene-expression series and five sequencing projects). Number of samples with usable processed profiles: unknown, because none are provided here.
plain_idea.predict: Cancer type, or whether a patient responded to checkpoint-inhibitor immunotherapy. The true answer would come from clinical records in each separate source study, recorded under different definitions of response.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Oncologists would like a cheap sequencing-based marker of who benefits from immunotherapy; but the field's flagship dataset was retracted for contamination, so the honest value here is a careful cross-study generalisation test rather than a new predictor.

ml_idea: None from this paper. A modelling project on tumour microbiomes would have to start from the primary resources the review points at (and reckon with the 2024 retraction of the Cancer Genome Atlas microbiome tables), not from anything this article supplies.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: there is no dataset to size. Rebuilding the cited third-party sequencing archives would mean terabytes of raw reads, which the project rules exclude.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement. It says 'No datasets were generated or analysed during the current study.' That is the whole evaluation, and it took one request.

verdict_reason: Narrative review, not a data paper. Fails Part A1: the data availability statement explicitly says no datasets were generated or analysed, the supplement contains only two copies of Figure 1, and there is no code or data repository. The accessions text-mined from it belong to other groups' published studies and are cited inside summary tables, so any target would have to be constructed from external raw sequencing (also failing A2 and A3). The underlying subfield is additionally hazardous: the best-known cancer-microbiome machine-learning dataset was retracted in 2024 over contamination.
